tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Analysing Dance Performance

questions.question: Q: What is the advantage of watching a live performance over a recorded one?
questions.correctAnswer: Live performance provides the full sensory experience — you feel the energy, scale and atmosphere in real time, and the audience-performer relationship is immediate and tangible.

questions.question: Q: Why is repeated viewing useful when analysing a recorded dance?
questions.correctAnswer: Repeated viewing lets you focus on different elements each time — first the overall structure, then specific movement details, design features or dancer relationships.

questions.question: Q: How do the four content categories help structure an analysis?
questions.correctAnswer: They provide a systematic framework so you cover all aspects: action (what), dynamics (how), space (where) and relationships (who), ensuring nothing is missed.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Analysing Dance Performance

questions.question: Q: Why should analysis always reference the choreographic intention?
questions.correctAnswer: Every choreographic choice serves the intention — linking your analysis to it shows you understand why decisions were made, not just what they are.

questions.question: Q: Name two design elements you should consider alongside movement when analysing a dance.
questions.correctAnswer: Costume and lighting — though set/staging and aural setting are also valid design elements that contribute to meaning.
